title: Does Vitamin C and E Supplementation Impair the Favorable Adaptations of Regular Exercise?
authors: Michalis G. Nikolaidis, Chad M. Kerksick, Manfred Lamprecht, Steven R. McAnulty
abstract: This study investigated whether vitamin C and E supplementation interferes with exercise adaptations. High doses of these vitamins are not recommended for exercising individuals due to conflicting evidence on their efficacy and potential harm.

title: Can supplementation with vitamin C and E alter physiological adaptations to strength training?
authors: Gøran Paulsen, Kristoffer T Cumming, Håvard Hamarsland, Elisabet Børsheim, Sveinung Berntsen, Truls ...
source: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
abstract: High doses of vitamins C and E were tested for their effects on strength training adaptations in young and older men. Supplementation blunted adaptations in young men but showed potential benefits in older men.

title: Effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on endogenous antioxidant systems and heat shock proteins in response to endurance training
authors: Kristoffer T. Cumming, Truls Raastad, Geir Holden, Nasser E. Bastani, Damaris Schneeberger, Maria Pa...
abstract: This study examined vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on antioxidant and heat shock protein systems during endurance training. Supplementation did not alter long-term training adaptations but increased acute exercise stress responses.

title: Vitamin C and E supplementation does not affect heat shock proteins or endogenous antioxidants in trained skeletal muscles during 12 weeks of strength training
authors: K. T. Cumming, T. Raastad, A. Sørstrøm, M. P. Paronetto, N. Mercatelli, I. Ugelstad, D. Caporossi, G...
abstract: This study examined the impact of vitamin C and E supplementation on trained individuals undergoing strength training. The supplementation did not alter acute exercise stress responses or long-term adaptations in heat shock proteins or endogenous antioxidants.

title: Vitamin C and E Supplementation Effects in Professional Soccer Players Under Regular Training
authors: Claudio C Zoppi, Rodrigo Hohl, Fernando C Silva, Fernanda L Lazarim, Joaquim MF Antunes Neto, Mirtes...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C and E supplementation in professional soccer players during training. Supplementation reduced lipid peroxidation and muscle damage but did not improve performance.

title: The Effect of Vitamins C and E Supplementation on Muscle Damage, Performance, and Body Composition in Athlete Women: A Clinical Trial
authors: Maryam Taghiyar, Reza Ghiasvand, Gholamreza Askari, Awat Feizi, Mitra Hariri, Nafiseh Shokri Mashhad...
abstract: This clinical trial examined the effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on muscle damage, performance, and body composition in trained female athletes over four weeks. The study found no significant improvements in any of these parameters due to the supplementation.

title: Effects of Acute Vitamin C plus Vitamin E Supplementation on Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage in Runners: A Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: María Martínez-Ferrán, Víctor Cuadrado-Peñafiel, Juan Manuel Sánchez-Andreo, Marta Villar-Lucas, Món...
abstract: This study investigated if vitamin C and E supplementation reduces exercise-induced muscle damage in runners. The supplementation did not significantly improve muscle damage markers or performance compared to a placebo.

title: The Effect of Vitamin C and E Supplementation on Muscle Damage and Oxidative Stress in Female Athletes: A Clinical Trial
authors: Maryam Taghiyar, Leila Darvishi, Gholamrez Askari, Awat Feizi, Mitra Hariri, Nafiseh Shokri Mashhadi...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on muscle damage and oxidative stress in female athletes. Results showed vitamin C and E supplementation reduced muscle damage and oxidative stress markers.

title: Effects of vitamins C and E supplementation combined with 12-week resistance training in older women with sarcopenia: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
authors: Xu Liu, Bo Chen, Yutian Jin, Feiyan Zhong, Yunjuan Zhang, Yu Li, Yun Zhang, Runhong Cui, Bing Wu, Cu...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of combined vitamin C, E, and resistance training in older women with sarcopenia. Supplementation with vitamins C and E enhanced muscle mass and strength gains compared to placebo.

title: Antioxidant Supplementation Impairs Changes in Body Composition Induced by Strength Training in Young Women
authors: MAURILIO T. DUTRA, SÁVIO ALEX, ALYSON F. SILVA, LEE E. BROWN, MARTIM BOTTARO
abstract: This study examined the effects of strength training with antioxidant supplementation on body composition in young women. Antioxidant supplementation impaired strength training-induced gains in fat-free mass and reductions in fat mass.

title: Vitamin C and E supplementation and high intensity interval training induced changes in lipid profile and haematological variables of young males
authors: Surojit Sarkar, Swapan Kr Dey, Gouriprosad Datta, Amit Bandyopadhyay
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on high-intensity interval training (HIIT) in young males. Supplementation protected against negative hematological changes and improved lipid profiles and explosive strength without affecting endurance.

title: Vitamin C, A and E supplementation decreases the expression of  HSPA1A  and  HSPB1  genes in the leukocytes of young polish figure skaters during a 10-day training camp
authors: Małgorzata Żychowska, Zbigniew Jastrzębski, Grzegorz Chruściński, Monika Michałowska–Sawczyn, Alicja...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study examined the effect of vitamin A, C, and E supplementation on gene expression in young figure skaters during a training camp. Supplementation significantly decreased the expression of stress-related genes HSPA1A and HSPB1 in leukocytes.

title: Elevated hepcidin serum level in response to inflammatory and iron signals in exercising athletes is independent of moderate supplementation with vitamin C and E
authors: Víctor Díaz, Ana B Peinado, Laura Barba-Moreno, Sandro Altamura, Javier Butragueño, Marcela González...
abstract: This study investigated hepcidin levels in athletes after exercise. Hepcidin remained elevated despite vitamin C and E supplementation, indicating these vitamins do not alter the response to inflammatory and iron signals.

title: Short-Term High-Dose Vitamin C and E Supplementation Attenuates Muscle Damage and Inflammatory Responses to Repeated Taekwondo Competitions: A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial
authors: Chun-Chung Chou, Yu-Chi Sung, Glen Davison, Chung-Yu Chen, Yi-Hung Liao
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on elite Taekwondo athletes. Supplementation attenuated muscle damage, hemolysis, and inflammatory responses to repeated competitions.

title: Vitamin C and E Treatment Blunts Sprint Interval Training–Induced Changes in Inflammatory Mediator-, Calcium-, and Mitochondria-Related Signaling in Recreationally Active Elderly Humans
authors: Victoria L. Wyckelsma, Tomas Venckunas, Marius Brazaitis, Stefano Gastaldello, Audrius Snieckus, Ner...
abstract: Sprint interval training in elderly individuals was studied with and without antioxidant treatment. Antioxidants blunted training-induced cellular signaling changes in muscle, but did not affect performance outcomes.

title: The effects of antioxidant vitamin supplementation on resistance exercise induced lipid peroxidation in trained and untrained participants
authors: Peter E Viitala, Ian J Newhouse, Norm LaVoie, Christine Gottardo
abstract: This study investigated the impact of vitamin E supplementation on exercise-induced lipid peroxidation in trained and untrained individuals. Vitamin E supplementation did not reduce oxidative damage, and training status did not affect lipid peroxidation levels post-exercise.

title: Exercise Training and Vitamin C Supplementation Affects Ferritin mRNA in Leukocytes without Affecting Prooxidative/Antioxidative Balance in Elderly Women
authors: Małgorzata Żychowska, Agata Grzybkowska, Monika Wiech, Robert Urbański, Wanda Pilch, Anna Piotrowska...
abstract: Exercise training with vitamin C supplementation decreased ferritin mRNA in elderly women's leukocytes. This intervention did not alter the prooxidative/antioxidative balance.

title: Differences in the Pro/Antioxidative Status and Cellular Stress Response in Elderly Women after 6 Weeks of Exercise Training Supported by 1000 mg of Vitamin C Supplementation
authors: Małgorzata Żychowska, Ewa Sadowska-Krępa, Elisabetta Damiani, Luca Tiano, Ewa Ziemann, Alicja Nowak-...
abstract: This study examined the effects of exercise training with vitamin C supplementation on antioxidant status and cellular stress response in elderly women. Vitamin C supplementation increased oxidative stress markers and influenced minor changes in gene expression related to training adaptation.

title: A Vitamin E-Enriched Antioxidant Diet Interferes with the Acute Adaptation of the Liver to Physical Exercise in Mice
authors: Miriam Hoene, Martin Irmler, Johannes Beckers, Martin Hrabě de Angelis, Hans-Ulrich Häring, Cora Wei...
abstract: A study examined how a vitamin E-enriched diet affects the liver's response to exercise in mice. High vitamin E intake disrupted the liver's normal metabolic and inflammatory adaptations to physical activity.

title: Vitamin C and E Treatment Blocks Changes in Kynurenine Metabolism Triggered by Three Weeks of Sprint Interval Training in Recreationally Active Elderly Humans
authors: Victoria L. Wyckelsma, Ada Trepci, Lilly Schwieler, Tomas Venckunas, Marius Brazaitis, Sigitas Kaman...
abstract: Sprint interval training in elderly men altered kynurenine pathway metabolism towards neuroprotection. This beneficial shift was prevented by concurrent vitamin C and E supplementation.

title: Influence of Vitamin C Supplementation on Oxidative Stress and Neutrophil Inflammatory Response in Acute and Regular Exercise
authors: Ljiljana M. Popovic, Nebojsa R. Mitic, Dijana Miric, Boban Bisevac, Mirjana Miric, Brankica Popovic
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C's impact on oxidative stress and neutrophil inflammation from exercise. Vitamin C supplementation reduced exercise-induced lipid peroxidation but did not affect neutrophil inflammatory response.

title: Supplementation with α-Lipoic Acid, CoQ10, and Vitamin E Augments Running Performance and Mitochondrial Function in Female Mice
authors: Arkan Abadi, Justin D. Crane, Daniel Ogborn, Bart Hettinga, Mahmood Akhtar, Andrew Stokl, Lauren Mac...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of an antioxidant cocktail on running performance and mitochondrial function in mice. The supplement improved performance and mitochondrial function in untrained female mice, but not in trained mice.

title: Enhanced Antioxidative Defense by Vitamins C and E Consumption Prevents 7-Day High-Salt Diet-Induced Microvascular Endothelial Function Impairment in Young Healthy Individuals
authors: Lidija Barić, Ines Drenjančević, Martina Mihalj, Anita Matić, Marko Stupin, Luka Kolar, Zrinka Mihal...
abstract: This study investigated if vitamins C and E prevent high-salt diet-induced microvascular dysfunction in healthy individuals. The findings show these vitamins prevented the diet's negative effects on endothelial function by mitigating oxidative stress.

title: Effect of high-dose vitamin C and E supplementation on muscle recovery and training adaptation: a mini review
authors: Jooyoung Kim
abstract: This review examined high-dose vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on exercise-induced muscle recovery and training adaptation. Evidence suggests potential negative impacts on adaptation, with unclear benefits for recovery.

title: Modification of the Effect of Vitamin E Supplementation on the Mortality of Male Smokers by Age and Dietary Vitamin C
authors: Harri Hemilä, Jaakko Kaprio
abstract: Vitamin E supplementation's effect on mortality in male smokers was examined. Its impact varied significantly by age and dietary vitamin C intake, suggesting heterogeneous effects in different population subgroups.

title: Do Antioxidant Vitamins Prevent Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage? A Systematic Review
authors: María Martinez-Ferran, Fabian Sanchis-Gomar, Carl J. Lavie, Giuseppe Lippi, Helios Pareja-Galeano
abstract: This systematic review examined vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on exercise-induced muscle damage. The available data are not conclusive regarding whether these vitamins prevent muscle damage.

title: Complex Effects of Vitamin E and Vitamin C Supplementation on  in Vitro  Neonatal Mononuclear Cell Responses to Allergens
authors: Heather J. H. Wassall, Graham Devereux, Anthony Seaton, Robert N. Barker
abstract: This study examined how vitamin E and C supplementation affects neonatal immune cells' response to allergens. Vitamin E showed complex effects, sometimes reducing proliferation and other times increasing it, while vitamin C had varied impacts on cytokine production.

title: The Effects of Strength Training Combined with Vitamin C and E Supplementation on Skeletal Muscle Mass and Strength: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: Maurilio T. Dutra, Wagner Rodrigues Martins, Alexandre L. A. Ribeiro, Martim Bottaro
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined studies on vitamin C and E supplementation combined with strength training. The findings suggest these supplements do not enhance muscle strength or mass and may even attenuate hypertrophy.

title: Potential harms of supplementation with high doses of antioxidants in athletes
authors: Shunchang Li, Babatunde Fasipe, Ismail Laher
abstract: This paper reviews the use of high-dose antioxidant supplements by athletes. It concludes that these supplements may hinder beneficial training adaptations and potentially cause harm.

title: The effects of multi mineral-vitamin D and vitamins (C+E) supplementation in the prevention of preeclampsia: An RCT
authors: Milad Azami, Tayebe Azadi, Sepidezahra Farhang, Shoobo Rahmati, Khadijeh Pourtaghi
abstract: A randomized trial investigated multimineral-vitamin D and vitamins C+E supplementation in pregnant women. Multimineral-vitamin D significantly reduced preeclampsia incidence and neonatal complications compared to controls.

title: Antioxidant supplements and endurance exercise: Current evidence and mechanistic insights
authors: Shaun A. Mason, Adam J. Trewin, Lewan Parker, Glenn D. Wadley
abstract: This review examines antioxidant supplements for endurance athletes. Most supplements lack evidence for performance enhancement, with some potentially hindering training adaptations.

title: Antioxidants and Exercise: A Redox-Informed Framework for Training Adaptation, Performance, and Recovery
authors: Dan Cristian Mănescu; Andrei Tudor; Andreea Maria Mănescu; Iulius Radulian Mărgărit; Cătălin Octavia...
abstract: Antioxidants can hinder training adaptations by blunting exercise-induced signals. However, certain food-derived antioxidants may aid recovery without impairing gains. A framework called Redox-Adaptive Periodization is proposed to optimize antioxidant use based on training goals.

title: Prior exercise and antioxidant supplementation: effect on oxidative stress and muscle injury
authors: Richard J Bloomer, Michael J Falvo, Brian K Schilling, Webb A Smith
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effects of prior eccentric exercise and antioxidant supplementation on muscle injury and oxidative stress in resistance-trained men. Neither intervention, alone or combined, significantly reduced markers of muscle injury or oxidative stress.

title: Effect of Vitamins A, C, and E Supplementation in the Treatment of Metabolic Syndrome in Albino Rats
authors: L. S. Bilbis, S. A. Muhammad, Y. Saidu, Y. Adamu
abstract: This study examined the effects of vitamins A, C, and E on metabolic syndrome in rats fed a high-salt diet. Vitamin supplementation significantly reduced blood pressure, improved lipid profiles, and increased antioxidant status, suggesting a protective role.

title: Controversies of antioxidant vitamins supplementation in exercise: ergogenic or ergolytic effects in humans?
authors: Cainara Lins Draeger, Andréia Naves, Natália Marques, Ana Beatriz Baptistella, Renata Alves Carnauba...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This commentary reviews recent studies on antioxidant vitamin supplementation and exercise-induced oxidative stress. Findings are controversial, with supplementation showing ergogenic, ergolytic, or no effects on physiological parameters and antioxidant enzyme activity.

title: Effect of vitamin E succinate on inflammatory cytokines induced by high-intensity interval training
authors: Hadi Sarir, Ghodsieh Emdadifard, Homayoun Farhangfar, Hossein TaheriChadorneshin
source: Journal of Research in Medical Sciences : The Official Journal of Isfahan University of Medical Sciences
abstract: This study investigated vitamin E succinate's effect on inflammatory cytokines after high-intensity interval training in rats. Vitamin E succinate supplementation reduced HIIT-induced increases in IL-6 and TNF-α.

title: Supplementation with Vitamins C and E and Exercise-Induced Delayed-Onset Muscle Soreness: A Systematic Review
authors: María F. Torre, María Martinez-Ferran, Néstor Vallecillo, Sergio L. Jiménez, Carlos Romero-Morales, ...
abstract: This systematic review examined vitamin C and E supplementation's effect on exercise-induced muscle soreness. The evidence is insufficient to confirm these vitamins minimize delayed-onset muscle soreness.

title: Mitigating the Growth, Biochemical Changes, Genotoxic and Pathological Effects of Copper Toxicity in Broiler Chickens by Supplementing Vitamins C and E
authors: Mohamed A. Hashem, Sahar S. Abd El Hamied, Eman M. A. Ahmed, Shimaa A. Amer, Mohamed E. El-Sharnouby
source: Animals : an Open Access Journal from MDPI
abstract: This study investigated the effects of copper sulfate toxicity and vitamin C/E supplementation on broiler chickens. Vitamins C and E, especially when combined, helped mitigate the negative impacts of copper toxicity on growth and liver health.

title: Prevention of Mammary Tumorigenesis in Acatalasemic Mice by Vitamin E Supplementation
authors: Kunihiko Ishii, Li‐Xue Zhen, Da‐hong Wang, Yuka Funamori, Katsuo Ogawa, Kazuhisa Taketa
source: Japanese Journal of Cancer Research : Gann
abstract: Acatalasemic mice were studied to assess vitamin E's effect on mammary tumors. Vitamin E supplementation significantly reduced mammary tumor incidence in these mice.

title: Vitamin E supplementation and pneumonia risk in males who initiated smoking at an early age: effect modification by body weight and dietary vitamin C
authors: Harri Hemilä, Jaakko Kaprio
abstract: This study examined vitamin E's effect on pneumonia risk in early-smoking males. Vitamin E increased pneumonia risk in underweight and very overweight smokers, especially those with high dietary vitamin C.

title: Combined effect of antioxidant supplementation and resistance training on oxidative stress markers, muscle and body composition in an elderly population
authors: F. Bobeuf; M. Labonte; I.J. Dionne; Abdelouahed Khalil
source: The Journal of Nutrition, Health & Aging
abstract: This study was aimed to examine the effect of vitamin C/E intake alone or combined with resistance training on antioxidant/pro-oxidant status, muscle strength and body composition in an elderly popula

title: Vitamin E Dietary Supplementation Improves Neurological Symptoms and Decreases c-Abl/p73 Activation in Niemann-Pick C Mice
authors: Tamara Marín, Pablo Contreras, Juan Francisco Castro, David Chamorro, Elisa Balboa, Mònica Bosch-Mor...
abstract: Dietary vitamin E supplementation was studied in Niemann-Pick C mice to assess its impact on neurological symptoms and disease progression. The supplementation delayed neurodegeneration, improved motor function, and reduced markers of oxidative stress and apoptosis.

title: Carbon tetrachloride-induced liver disease in rats: the potential effect of supplement oils with vitamins E and C on the nutritional status
authors: Rasha S. A. Ismail, Ashraf A. A. El-Megeid, Aly R. Abdel-Moemin
abstract: This study investigated the effects of different oils and vitamin supplementation on carbon tetrachloride-induced liver damage in rats. Supplementing oils with vitamins E and C, particularly flaxseed oil, significantly improved liver function and histology.

title: Antioxidant Effects and Insulin Resistance Improvement of Chromium Combined with Vitamin C and E Supplementation for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
authors: Ming-Hoang Lai
source: Journal of Clinical Biochemistry and Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effects of chromium, vitamin C, and E supplementation on type 2 diabetes patients. Combined supplementation significantly reduced oxidative stress and improved glucose metabolism.

title: The Effect of Combined Vitamin C and Vitamin E Supplementation on Oxidative Stress Markers in Women with Endometriosis: A Randomized, Triple-Blind Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial
authors: Leila Amini, Razieh Chekini, Mohammad Reza Nateghi, Hamid Haghani, Tannaz Jamialahmadi, Thozhukat Sa...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of combined vitamin C and E supplementation on oxidative stress and pain in women with endometriosis. The supplementation significantly reduced oxidative stress markers and pelvic pain symptoms.

title: Antioxidants and Sports Performance
authors: Vicente Javier Clemente-Suárez, Álvaro Bustamante-Sanchez, Juan Mielgo-Ayuso, Ismael Martínez-Guarda...
abstract: This review analyzes the role of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and antioxidant responses in sports performance and training adaptations. ROS production during exercise significantly impacts performance, and antioxidants can aid recovery and performance.

title: Associations of serum levels of vitamins A, C, and E with the risk of cognitive impairment among elderly Koreans
authors: Sung Hee Kim, Yeong Mi Park, Bo Youl Choi, Mi Kyung Kim, Sungwon Roh, Kyunga Kim, Yoon Jung Yang
abstract: This study examined serum vitamin levels and cognitive impairment risk in elderly Koreans. Higher beta-gamma tocopherol levels were associated with a reduced risk of cognitive impairment, particularly in men and non-smokers.

title: Combination of vitamin E and vitamin C alleviates renal function in hyperoxaluric rats via antioxidant activity
authors: Orapun JATURAKAN, Thasinas DISSAYABUTRA, Narongsak CHAIYABUTR, Anusak KIJTAWORNRAT, Piyaratana TOSUK...
source: The Journal of Veterinary Medical Science
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin E and C on hyperoxaluric rats. Combined vitamin E and C supplementation protected against oxalate-induced kidney damage by reducing oxidative stress.

title: Vitamin C Protects from Impairment of Memory Induced by E-Cigarette Aerosol Exposure
authors: Karem H. Alzoubi, Omar F. Khabour, Nour Al-Sawalha, Enaam M. Al Momany, Anan Jarab, Razan Haddad, Na...
abstract: This study investigated if Vitamin C protects rats from memory impairment caused by e-cigarette aerosol exposure. Vitamin C prevented memory deficits and restored oxidative stress markers and BDNF levels.

title: Excessive Vitamin E Supplementation: Implications for Ovarian Physiology and Reproductive Health
authors: Farzaneh Rabiee, Masoud Fattahi, Mohammad Iranzad, Mohsen Rahimi Andani, Farnoosh Jafarpour, Mohamma...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of different vitamin E doses on mouse reproductive health. Excessive vitamin E supplementation impaired fertility, oocyte and embryo development, and ovarian function by altering oxidative stress markers.

title: Antioxidants and Skeletal Muscle Performance: “Common Knowledge” vs. Experimental Evidence
authors: Andrés Hernández, Arthur Cheng, Håkan Westerblad
abstract: This paper reviews experimental evidence on the effects of antioxidants on skeletal muscle performance. Findings suggest that common beliefs about antioxidant benefits may not be supported by scientific data and could potentially be harmful.

title: International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: effects of dietary antioxidants on exercise and sports performance
authors: Drew E. Gonzalez; Broderick L. Dickerson; Brandon M. Roberts; Jennifer A. Kurtz; Hunter S. Waldman; ...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: Following a comprehensive review, the International Society of Sports Nutrition (ISSN) has developed an official position on the role of dietary antioxidants in exercise and sport. Antioxidants play a

title: Vitamin E Supplementation Delays Cellular Senescence  In Vitro
authors: Giorgio La Fata, Nicole Seifert, Peter Weber, M. Hasan Mohajeri
abstract: This study investigated vitamin E's effect on cellular senescence in human cells. Vitamin E supplementation reduced senescent cells by downregulating P21 expression.

title: Exercise-Induced Oxidative Stress and Dietary Antioxidants
authors: Abbas Yavari, Maryam Javadi, Parvin Mirmiran, Zahra Bahadoran
abstract: This review examined evidence on antioxidant supplementation and exercise-induced oxidative stress. A balanced diet rich in natural antioxidants is recommended over supplementation for athletes.

title: Vitamin Supplementation in Sports: A Decade of Evidence-Based Insights
authors: Magdalena Wiacek, Emilia Nowak, Piotr Lipka, Remigiusz Denda, Igor Z. Zubrzycki
abstract: This review synthesizes a decade of research on vitamin supplementation in athletes. Vitamin D deficiency is common, and while some vitamins aid performance, supplementation should be individualized and based on confirmed deficiencies.

title: Supplementation of Underfed Twin-Bearing Ewes with Herbal Vitamins C and E: Impacts on Birth Weight, Postnatal Growth, and Pre-Weaning Survival of the Lambs
authors: Víctor H. Parraguez, Francisco Sales, Oscar A. Peralta, Eileen Narbona, Raúl Lira, Mónica De los Rey...
source: Animals : an Open Access Journal from MDPI
abstract: Herbal vitamins C and E, alone or with concentrate, were supplemented to underfed twin-bearing ewes. Supplementation improved lamb birth weight and antioxidant capacity, with combined treatment showing the best results.

title: A metabolomic investigation of the effects of vitamin E supplementation in humans
authors: Max Wong, John K Lodge
abstract: This study investigated plasma metabolome changes after vitamin E supplementation in healthy males. Vitamin E supplementation altered lysophosphatidylcholine levels, suggesting an influence on phospholipid metabolism.

title: Effects of Vitamin C Supplementation on Plasma and Urinary Vitamin C Concentration in Korean Women
authors: Jayoung Choi, Do-Yeon Kim, Ryowon Choue, Hyunjung Lim
abstract: This study investigated the effects of 100 mg and 2,000 mg vitamin C supplements on Korean women. Both doses increased plasma and urinary vitamin C, with the higher dose reducing oxidative stress and the lower dose reducing fatigue.

title: Effects of ascorbic acid supplementation on oxidative stress markers in healthy women following a single bout of exercise
authors: Manita Yimcharoen, Suwatsin Kittikunnathum, Chawannut Suknikorn, Wichuda Nak-on, Petcharee Yeethong,...
abstract: This study investigated ascorbic acid's effects on oxidative stress markers in women after exercise. Ascorbic acid improved antioxidant capacity but did not prevent exercise-induced muscle damage.

title: Marginal vitamin C status is associated with reduced fat oxidation during submaximal exercise in young adults
authors: Carol S Johnston, Corinne Corte, Pamela D Swan
abstract: Marginal vitamin C status was studied in relation to fat oxidation during submaximal exercise. Low vitamin C status was associated with reduced fat oxidation, which was improved by vitamin C repletion.

title: Effect of vitamins C or E supplementation to Tris diluent on the semen quality of Awassi rams preserved at 5 ˚C
authors: Osama Ibrahim Azawi, Elias Khudhur Hussein
abstract: This study investigated the effect of adding vitamins C or E to a semen diluent for Awassi rams stored at 5°C. Adding vitamins C or E improved sperm motility, viability, and reduced abnormalities during storage.

title: Association of vitamin C, vitamin D, vitamin E and risk of bladder cancer: a dose-response meta-analysis
authors: Fuqiang Chen, Qingshu Li, Yang Yu, Wenrong Yang, Fei Shi, Yan Qu
abstract: This meta-analysis examined the link between vitamins C, D, and E and bladder cancer risk. Higher vitamin D and E intake, particularly alpha-tocopherol, may reduce risk, while gamma-tocopherol might increase it, with effects more pronounced in smokers.

title: Exercise performance and physiological responses: the potential role of redox imbalance
authors: Kavey Vidal, Nathaniel Robinson, Stephen J. Ives
abstract: This study investigated the effects of hyperoxia and an antioxidant cocktail on cycling performance and physiological responses. Ingesting an antioxidant cocktail impaired performance, ventilation, and economy, suggesting a disruption of redox balance.

title: Effect of an 8-weeks aerobic training program in elderly on oxidative stress and Hsp72 expression in leukocytes during antioxidant supplementation
authors: David Simar; D. Malatesta; E. Mas; M. Delage; C. Caillaud
source: The Journal of Nutrition, Health & Aging
abstract: To investigate the effect of aerobic training in the context of antioxidant supplementation on systemic oxidative stress and leukocytes heat shock protein (Hsp)72 expression in the elderly. Sixteen se

title: Resistance-Trained Individuals Are Less Susceptible to Oxidative Damage after Eccentric Exercise
authors: Ypatios Spanidis, Dimitrios Stagos, Christina Papanikolaou, Konstantina Karatza, Andria Theodosi, Ar...
abstract: Resistance-trained individuals experienced less oxidative damage and had a stronger antioxidant profile after eccentric exercise compared to untrained individuals. This suggests training status significantly influences exercise-induced oxidative stress and recovery.

title: Vitamin C and glutathione supplementation: a review of their additive effects on exercise performance
authors: Eunjoo Lee, Hun-Young Park, Sung-Woo Kim, Jisu Kim, Kiwon Lim
abstract: This review examined vitamin C and glutathione supplementation's effects on exercise performance. Combined supplementation's additive effects are anticipated but remain largely unexplored and require further study.

title: The effect of an acute antioxidant supplementation compared with placebo on performance and hormonal response during a high volume resistance training session
authors: James Ackerman, Tom Clifford, Lars R McNaughton, David J Bentley
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: An antioxidant supplement was compared to a placebo before a high-volume resistance training session. The antioxidant group showed improved muscle performance and a blunted growth hormone response.

title: Laying performance, digestibility and plasma hormones in laying hens exposed to chronic heat stress as affected by betaine, vitamin C, and/or vitamin E supplementation
authors: Youssef A. Attia, Abd El-Hamid E. Abd El-Hamid, Ahmed A. Abedalla, Marfat A. Berika, Mohammed A. Al-...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of betaine, vitamin C, and vitamin E supplementation on laying hens under chronic heat stress. Vitamin C supplementation showed the greatest improvement in laying performance and combatted heat stress effects.

title: Proteome-Driven Elucidation of Adaptive Responses
authors: to Combined Vitamin E and C Deficiency in Zebrafish
abstract: This study investigated the proteomic changes in zebrafish due to combined vitamin E and C deficiency. Vitamin C deficiency, especially with vitamin E deficiency, induces stress responses and shifts cellular energy metabolism.

title: Exercise-Induced Oxidative Stress and the Effects of Antioxidant Intake from a Physiological Viewpoint
authors: Takuji Kawamura, Isao Muraoka
abstract: This review examines exercise-induced oxidative stress and the impact of antioxidant intake in healthy individuals. It finds that while exercise increases reactive oxygen species, antioxidant supplementation's effects are extensively studied but complex.

title: Dietary and supplemental intake of vitamins C and E is associated with altered DNA methylation in an epigenome-wide association study meta-analysis
authors: Amena Keshawarz, Roby Joehanes, Jiantao Ma, Gha Young Lee, Ricardo Costeira, Pei-Chien Tsai, Olatz M...
abstract: This study meta-analyzed EWAS results to assess vitamin C and E intake's association with DNA methylation. Vitamin C intake was linked to numerous CpG sites, potentially influencing systems development and immune response.

title: Tissue-Specific Effects of Vitamin E Supplementation
authors: Eugene Jansen, Dale Viezeliene, Piet Beekhof, Eric Gremmer, Leonid Ivanov
abstract: A study supplemented mice with varying vitamin E doses, including a high dose (25× RDI). High vitamin E intake showed beneficial effects in male mouse livers but caused toxicity and inflammation in male mouse kidneys.

title: Dietary thiols in exercise: oxidative stress defence, exercise performance, and adaptation
authors: Yanita McLeay, Stephen Stannard, Stuart Houltham, Carlene Starck
abstract: This paper reviews dietary thiols, focusing on their role in exercise-induced oxidative stress defense and performance. It suggests that thiol donors, like keratin, may enhance antioxidant capacity and performance without negatively impacting training adaptations.

title: Haptoglobin Phenotype, Preeclampsia Risk and the Efficacy of Vitamin C and E Supplementation to Prevent Preeclampsia in a Racially Diverse Population
authors: Tracey L. Weissgerber, Robin E. Gandley, Paula L. McGee, Catherine Y. Spong, Leslie Myatt, Kenneth J...
abstract: This study investigated haptoglobin phenotype, preeclampsia risk, and vitamin supplementation efficacy. No association was found between haptoglobin phenotype and preeclampsia risk or vitamin efficacy, except for increased risk in Hispanic Hp 2-2 women.

title: Vitamin A Oral Supplementation Induces Oxidative Stress and Suppresses IL-10 and HSP70 in Skeletal Muscle of Trained Rats
authors: Lyvia Lintzmaier Petiz, Carolina Saibro Girardi, Rafael Calixto Bortolin, Alice Kunzler, Juciano Gas...
abstract: Vitamin A supplementation was studied in trained rats. It impaired exercise-induced antioxidant capacity and suppressed anti-inflammatory responses in skeletal muscle.

title: Radioiodine-induced oxidative stress in patients with differentiated thyroid carcinoma and effect of supplementation with vitamins C and E and selenium (antioxidants)
authors: Pedro Weslley Rosário, Kelly Cristina Siqueira Batista, Maria Regina Calsolari
abstract: Radioiodine therapy for thyroid cancer was studied for its oxidative stress effects. Antioxidant supplementation significantly reduced this stress.

title: A blinded, placebo‐controlled study on the clinical effects of vitamin E supplementation in dogs with osteoarthritis
authors: Casey L. Gordon, Samantha J. Reeves, Richard K. Burchell, Craig Thomson, Arnon Gal, Nicolas Lopez‐Vi...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin E supplementation in dogs with osteoarthritis. Vitamin E did not improve pain, lameness, quality of life, or reduce pain medication needs.

title: Oligomerized lychee fruit extract (OLFE) and a mixture of vitamin C and vitamin E for endurance capacity in a double blind randomized controlled trial
authors: Seung Wan Kang, Seokyung Hahn, Jung-Kyu Kim, Seung-Min Yang, Byung-Joo Park, Sang Chul Lee
abstract: Oligomerized lychee fruit extract (OLFE) and a vitamin C/E mixture were tested for endurance effects in exercising males. OLFE significantly improved running time and anaerobic threshold, while the vitamin mixture unexpectedly reduced VO2 max.

title: The association of oxidative stress of neonatal hyperbilirubinemia and vitamin E supplementation
authors: Mohamed Zaeim Hafez Ahmed, Reham Helmy Amin Helmy Saad, Ahmad Gadalla, Ramadan Hassan Ibrahim Thabet...
abstract: This study investigated the effect of vitamin E supplementation on neonatal hyperbilirubinemia treated with phototherapy. Vitamin E significantly reduced serum bilirubin levels and the duration of phototherapy.

title: Vitamin C may alleviate exercise-induced bronchoconstriction: a meta-analysis
authors: Harri Hemilä
abstract: This meta-analysis examined if vitamin C affects exercise-induced bronchoconstriction. Vitamin C administration significantly reduced post-exercise FEV1 decline and the proportion of participants experiencing EIB.

title: Comparison of the effects of two antioxidant diets on oxidative stress markers in triathletes
authors: Claudia D. Schneider, Patricia M. Bock, Georgia F. Becker, Jose Claudio F. Moreira, Adriane Bello-Kl...
abstract: This study compared the effects of regular and high antioxidant diets on oxidative stress markers in triathletes. A high antioxidant diet improved several markers of redox status in the athletes.

title: Prevention of Teratogenesis in Pregnancies of Obese Rats by Vitamin E Supplementation
authors: Martin Alcala, Victoria E. Bolado, Isabel Sánchez-Vera, Sonia Clapés, Francisco Dasí, Guillermo Sáez...
abstract: Obese rats were supplemented with vitamin E to investigate its effect on teratogenesis. Vitamin E prevented malformations by maintaining maternal glutathione levels, which protected embryos from oxidative stress.

title: Antioxidant Supplementation Hinders the Role of Exercise Training as a Natural Activator of SIRT1
authors: Carmine Sellitto, Graziamaria Corbi, Berenice Stefanelli, Valentina Manzo, Marta Trucillo, Bruno Cha...
abstract: Exercise training increases SIRT1 levels, which boosts the body's antioxidant system. However, antioxidant supplements appear to interfere with this exercise-induced activation of SIRT1.

title: Vitamin 25(OH)D 3 , E, and C Supplementation Impact the Inflammatory and Antioxidant Responses in Piglets Fed a Deoxynivalenol-Contaminated Diet and Challenged with Lipopolysaccharides
authors: Béatrice Sauvé, Younes Chorfi, Marie-Pierre Létourneau-Montminy, Frédéric Guay
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin 25(OH)D₃, E, and C supplementation on piglets fed a deoxynivalenol-contaminated diet and challenged with lipopolysaccharides. Vitamins E and C, or all three vitamins, protected against deoxynivalenol by reducing oxidative stress and inflammation.

title: Can Low-Dose of Dietary Vitamin E Supplementation Reduce Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage and Oxidative Stress? A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: Myunghee Kim, Hyeyoon Eo, Josephine Gahyun Lim, Hyunjung Lim, Yunsook Lim
abstract: This meta-analysis examined the effects of vitamin E supplementation on exercise-induced muscle damage. Low-dose vitamin E, especially under 500 IU, was found to reduce muscle damage, particularly in athletes.

title: Oxidative Stress, Mitochondrial Function and Adaptation to Exercise: New Perspectives in Nutrition
authors: Nancy Vargas-Mendoza, Marcelo Angeles-Valencia, Ángel Morales-González, Eduardo Osiris Madrigal-Sant...
abstract: This paper reviews how mitochondria adapt to exercise-induced energy demands and oxidative stress. It explores whether nutrients, particularly antioxidants, might interfere with this adaptation or exercise performance.

title: Resistance-based training improves mitochondrial capacity and redox balance in aging adults, independent of polyphenol supplementation
authors: Mathias Flensted-Jensen, Cecilie Moe Weinreich, Ann-Sofie Kleis-Olsen, Filip Hansen, Nadia Stenner S...
abstract: Resistance training improved mitochondrial capacity and redox balance in older adults. Polyphenol supplementation did not enhance these adaptations and may have altered some vitamin responses.

title: Vitamin E (α-tocopherol) supplementation in diabetic rats: effects on the proximal colon
authors: Luciana P Roldi, Renata VF Pereira, Eleandro A Tronchini, Gabriela V Rizo, Célia R Scoaris, Jacqueli...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin E supplementation on the proximal colons of diabetic rats. Vitamin E (2%) reduced blood sugar and protected myenteric neurons, but did not alter intestinal wall structure.

title: Redox correlation in muscle lengthening and immune response in eccentric exercise
authors: Feng He, Chia-Chen Chuang, Tingyang Zhou, Qing Jiang, Darlene A. Sedlock, Li Zuo
abstract: Eccentric exercise in mice and humans was studied for its effects on muscle function and immune cells. Antioxidant supplementation attenuated exercise-induced changes in anti-apoptotic proteins and may protect against muscle dysfunction.

title: Effect of vitamin E supplementation on chicken sperm quality: A meta-analysis
authors: Sari Yanti Hayanti, Cecep Hidayat, Anuraga Jayanegara, Mohammad Miftakhus Sholikin, Supardi Rusdiana...
abstract: This meta-analysis examined the effect of dietary vitamin E on rooster sperm quality. Vitamin E supplementation significantly improved sperm concentration, motility, viability, and fertility, while reducing sperm death.

title: Effect of Antioxidant Supplementation on NET Formation Induced by LPS In Vitro; the Roles of Vitamins E and C, Glutathione, and N-acetyl Cysteine
authors: Germán Muñoz-Sánchez, Lucila A. Godínez-Méndez, Mary Fafutis-Morris, Vidal Delgado-Rizo
abstract: This study investigated how antioxidant supplementation affects LPS-induced NET formation in neutrophils. Antioxidant combinations significantly reduced NET formation and oxidative stress markers in vitro.

title: Vitamin C and E antioxidant supplementation may significantly reduce pain symptoms in endometriosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
authors: Patrick Bayu *, Jacobus Jeno Wibisono
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined the efficacy of vitamin C and E supplementation for endometriosis pain. The findings suggest that this antioxidant combination significantly reduces chronic pelvic pain, dysmenorrhea, and dyspareunia compared to placebo.

title: Acute exercise and oxidative stress: a 30 year history
authors: Kelsey Fisher-Wellman, Richard J Bloomer
abstract: Acute exercise can induce oxidative stress, with its extent influenced by exercise and subject factors. This stress, however, appears to be a necessary stimulus for enhancing endogenous antioxidant defenses.

title: Metabolomic Analysis of Vitamin E Supplement Use in the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial
authors: Jungeun Lim, Hyokyoung G. Hong, Stephanie J. Weinstein, Mary C. Playdon, Amanda J. Cross, Rachael St...
abstract: This study analyzed serum metabolomic profiles in relation to vitamin E dosages from a cancer screening trial. Vitamin E supplementation was associated with changes in various metabolites, including steroid hormones, with sex-specific differences observed.

title: Effect of Antioxidant Supplementation on Markers of Oxidative Stress and Muscle Damage after Strength Exercise: A Systematic Review
authors: Cristina Canals-Garzón, Rafael Guisado-Barrilao, Darío Martínez-García, Ignacio Jesús Chirosa-Ríos, ...
abstract: This systematic review examined antioxidant supplementation's effects on oxidative stress and muscle damage after strength exercise. Antioxidants like pomegranate juice and taurine showed beneficial effects, potentially reducing fatigue and speeding recovery.

title: Effects of vitamin E supplementation on sow gestation: a meta-analysis
authors: Ni Wayan Helpina Widyasanti, Sari Yanti Hayanti, Cecep Hidayat, I. Putu Cahyadi Putra, Jonathan Anug...
abstract: This meta-analysis evaluated vitamin E supplementation in pregnant sows. Vitamin E significantly increased serum α-tocopherol in sows and piglets, but did not affect litter size or weight.

title: Exercise Training and Skeletal Muscle Antioxidant Enzymes: An Update
authors: Scott K. Powers, Erica Goldstein, Matthew Schrager, Li Li Ji
abstract: This review summarizes how endurance, interval, and resistance exercise training increase skeletal muscle antioxidant enzymes. This upregulation protects against exercise-induced oxidative damage, potentially delaying fatigue and improving performance.

title: The effect of supplementation with vitamins A, B, C, D, and E on disease severity and inflammatory responses in patients with COVID-19: a randomized clinical trial
authors: Mohammad Taghi Beigmohammadi, Sama Bitarafan, Azin Hoseindokht, Alireza Abdollahi, Laya Amoozadeh, D...
abstract: This study investigated the impact of vitamin A, B, C, D, and E supplementation on COVID-19 patients in the ICU. Vitamin supplementation improved inflammatory markers and disease severity, but did not significantly affect mortality or prolonged hospitalization after adjustments.
